solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Swimmers in bore by wharves

indicators.note: by means next to, so the wharves sit beside the first piece

parts.note: to bear a child is to have it, so bore can mean had
docks are wharves where ships tie up

explanation.surface: Fish turn up in a tidal bore running past the quayside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a tidal wave or a dull person, but it is the past tense of bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Haddock are North Atlantic food fish, so a group of them are swimmers.

clue.text: Missing daughter is increasingly weak- minded — that's concerning

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so one letter is omitted

parts.note: dafter means sillier, more daft

explanation.surface: With the daughter gone, a parent is becoming more feeble, which is worrying.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask after someone is to ask concerning or about them.

clue.text: Instruments for drawing ship waves with advanced drag

indicators.note: waves as a verb suggests things being tossed about, mixing the letters

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: A vessel's wake and its drag are recorded by drafting devices.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagraph is a device for copying or enlarging drawings, a draughting tool.

clue.text: Example of Lewis gun initially seen as a weapon

parts.note: C S Lewis, author of the Narnia books, is one Lewis

indicators.note: initially means the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A Lewis gun is first regarded as a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lewis gun is a real First World War machine gun, which hides the author C S Lewis.
explanation.definitionFit: CS gas is a tear gas used as a riot-control agent.

clue.text: Develop in audition, at the home of conceited youth

indicators.note: in audition means as heard, a sound-alike signal

parts.words: at the home of conceited youth
parts.note: chez is French for at the home of; a pup is a cheeky or conceited young man

explanation.surface: Someone tries out for a part in the house of an arrogant young man.
explanation.walkthrough: Chez is said 'shay', so CHEZ PUP is heard as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To shape up is to develop or progress in a particular way.

clue.text: Revolutionary sport in fine Asian city

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the whole construction is read backwards
in places the sport inside the word for fine

parts.note: OK means fine, all right
to toy with something is to sport or play with it

explanation.surface: An insurgent pastime takes place in a pleasant city in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: To sport with something is to toy with it, which is why sport gives a plaything word.
explanation.definitionFit: Kyoto is the former imperial capital of Japan, a major city in Asia.

clue.text: Link displayed by King riding horse wearing Queen's monogram

indicators.note: riding means sitting on top of, so the king precedes the horse in a down clue

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
an Arab is a breed of horse
in means wearing, as in in uniform
ER (Elizabeth Regina) was the monogram of Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A king on horseback wears a royal emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: A karabiner is a metal clip with a spring gate used by climbers to connect ropes.

clue.text: Old geeks ousting Germany's experts

indicators.note: ousting means expelling, so a letter is driven out

parts.note: nerds are geeks
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: Elderly tech enthusiasts push out the German specialists.
explanation.definitionFit: Oner is British slang for someone outstanding at something, an ace.

clue.text: Even lady in opposition brings chap from secret society

parts.note: in opposition: odd is the opposite of even
fellow, a man, is taken as the opposite of lady

explanation.surface: A lady sitting in the opposition benches brings along a member of a secret group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in opposition' applies to both words: each is replaced by its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oddfellow is a member of the Oddfellows, a fraternal friendly society with secret rituals.

clue.text: Fly back having absorbed western accent

indicators.note: having absorbed means taking another letter inside
back tells us to read the insect's name from right to left

parts.note: a gnat is a small fly

explanation.surface: An insect returns, having picked up a cowboy's drawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns GNAT into TANG, and 'having absorbed' puts W inside it after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is a nasal quality of speech, a regional manner of pronunciation.

clue.text: Make public where Jack is likely to go in Berks?

parts.note: to air an opinion is to make it public

parts.words: where Jack is likely to go
parts.note: Jack (Jack Tar) is a sailor, and the heads are a ship's toilets

explanation.surface: Someone wonders aloud where a man named Jack might end up in Berkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Berks looks like the abbreviation for Berkshire, an English county, but it is British slang: a berk is a fool. The question mark flags that wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Airheads are empty-headed, foolish people, just like berks in British slang.

clue.text: Black run — again and again it's freezing

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
the abbreviation for run is used again
and once more, a third time

explanation.surface: A skier on a black (expert) slope keeps going down and finds it cold.
explanation.walkthrough: A black run is the hardest ski slope; here it is just B and R, and 'again and again' adds two more Rs.
explanation.definitionFit: Brrr is the shivering exclamation people make when they feel very cold.

clue.text: Gradually, flight holding times upset Paddy

indicators.note: holding means the flight of stairs contains the next piece

parts.note: a flight is a set of steps
times as in multiplication, three by four

indicators.note: upset in a down clue would be turned over; here it means the word is reversed

parts.note: a paddy is a fit of temper, as is a pet

explanation.surface: Slowly climbing a staircase, someone repeatedly upsets an Irishman.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddy looks like a nickname for an Irishman, but here it is a tantrum; 'times' is the by of multiplication.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something step by step means doing it in gradual stages.

clue.text: Payment system shot even if secure

parts.note: a chip is a short lofted shot in golf
and is an archaic word for if or even if
to pin something is to secure it

explanation.surface: A payment method is described as hopeless even when it is safe.
explanation.walkthrough: AND in the old sense 'if' is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Chip and PIN is the card scheme where a microchip card is verified by a personal number.

clue.text: Organ donated by curt tough female

indicators.note: curt means short, so the word is cut by its last letter

parts.note: hard means tough
Monica is a female name

explanation.surface: An organ is donated by a brusque, hard woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Organ suggests a body part for donation, but it is the mouth organ.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonica is also called a mouth organ, a small wind instrument.

clue.text: Cleaner wants empty bath and urinals dealt with

indicators.note: dealt with, like cards dealt out, means the letters are redistributed
empty means the inside letters are removed, leaving the outer ones

explanation.surface: A cleaning worker needs an empty tub and the gents sorted.
explanation.definitionFit: A nailbrush is a small brush for scrubbing fingernails, a cleaning tool.

clue.text: Artful plonker's out of line

indicators.note: out of means one letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: plonker and willy are both British slang for the penis

explanation.surface: A fool is said to be behaving improperly.
explanation.walkthrough: Plonker also means an idiot in British slang, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: Wily means crafty and cunning, which is what artful means.

clue.text: Eddy's both hands in trendy fleece gloves?

definitions.note: Eddy's here is eddy plus is: the answer is a noun meaning eddy

indicators.note: gloves as a verb means encases, so the fleece wraps round the rest

parts.note: fleece is sheep's wool

indicators.note: in places the hands inside the trendy word

parts.note: hip means trendy
R and L stand for right and left hands

explanation.surface: A man called Eddy wears woolly fashionable gloves on both hands.
explanation.walkthrough: Eddy looks like a man's name, but it is a swirl of water; the question mark flags the odd picture of fleece wearing gloves.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirlpool is a swirling mass of water, a large eddy.

clue.text: Mars Bars best, essentially

indicators.note: essentially points to the central, essential letters of each word

explanation.surface: A claim that Mars chocolate bars are the best ones.
explanation.walkthrough: Mars looks like the chocolate bar brand, but it is the Roman god of war.
explanation.definitionFit: Ares is the Greek god of war, the counterpart of the Roman deity.

clue.text: Assesses wannabe wits? I never bothered

indicators.note: bothered means flustered and in disarray, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A recruiter wonders whether hopeful comedians are funny, admitting they never cared.
explanation.definitionFit: An employer interviews an applicant to evaluate a would-be candidate.

clue.text: Wingless ant bumped by winged insect in very small grass

indicators.note: bumped by means displaced or ousted by the replacement

parts.note: tiny means very small

indicators.note: wingless means stripped of its sides, leaving the middle letter

parts.note: a moth is a winged insect

explanation.surface: A tiny ant without wings is knocked over by a flying bug in the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wingless' reduces ANT to N; in TINY, MOTH takes its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Timothy is a meadow grass grown for hay and fodder.

clue.text: Peg so, so angry about bad reaction to stress

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the next piece
angry suggests agitation, so these letters are stirred up

parts.note: bum is slang for bad or poor quality, as in a bum deal

explanation.surface: Someone named Peg is so cross about a poor reaction to pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of PEGSOSO gives GOOSEPS, and 'about' wraps it round BUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Goosebumps are raised skin bumps caused by fear or cold, a bodily response to alarm.

clue.text: Quiet chief points across vacated hut

indicators.note: across means stretched over, so it spans the next piece

parts.note: the sum of something is its gist or chief points

indicators.note: vacated means emptied of the middle, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: A leader indicates silence across an empty shed.
explanation.definitionFit: Shtum is Yiddish-derived British slang for silent, keeping one's mouth shut.

clue.text: Photograph primates raised around India

indicators.note: around means the reversed word surrounds the next letter
raised in a down clue means lifted upwards, read bottom to top

parts.note: apes are primates
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A snapshot shows monkeys reared around India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses APES to SEPA, and 'around' wraps it about I.
explanation.definitionFit: A sepia is a brownish old-fashioned print, a photo in that tone.

clue.text: I'll be found on large toy

indicators.note: be found on means placed after, in an across clue written to the right

parts.note: L is the clothing abbreviation for large
I is one's self, the ego; the surface reads it as I will

explanation.surface: A child declares they will be found sitting on a big toy.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the I of 'I'll' matters: the self is the ego.
explanation.definitionFit: Lego is the brand of interlocking plastic building bricks for children.

clue.text: Depression's new for space pioneer

parts.note: a glen is a narrow valley, a depression in the land; the 's means has

explanation.surface: Someone's low mood has a fresh source for an astronaut.
explanation.walkthrough: Depression suggests gloom; it is a hollow in the landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: John Glenn was the first American astronaut to orbit the Earth, in 1962.

clue.text: Suspect former PM mostly limited by dimness

indicators.note: limited by means hemmed in on both sides by the following piece

parts.note: mist causes dimness of vision

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: Liz Truss was briefly UK Prime Minister in 2022

explanation.surface: A short-lived former Prime Minister is viewed with suspicion through a fog.
explanation.walkthrough: Liz Truss was UK Prime Minister for only about seven weeks in 2022, fitting a clue that cuts her short.
explanation.definitionFit: To mistrust someone is to doubt them, so the verb matches suspect.

clue.text: Strong acid may score this buzz

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as two words
second meaning: to give someone a buzz is to ring them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' suggests etching, but it means register a rating on a scale.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a buzz is informal for calling them on the telephone.

clue.text: Dancing girl sham lawyer holds over

indicators.note: over means turned the other way, so the concealed letters run backwards
holds means the letters are contained within these words

explanation.surface: A fake solicitor keeps hold of a dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds over' does two jobs: hiding inside 'sham lawyer' and reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An almah is an Egyptian female performer, a professional entertainer who sings and dances.

clue.text: Foal, perhaps playing, angrily biting mare's tail

indicators.note: biting means holding a letter between the teeth, so the shuffled letters close round it
playing means moving about freely, so the letters are rearranged
tail means the final letter of the word is the one used

parts.note: taken as the word mare itself

explanation.surface: A frisky foal snaps crossly at a mare's tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges angrily as YARLING, and 'biting' takes the final E of mare inside it after the Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearling is a horse in its second year; a foal, perhaps, grows into one.
